rumours: Three silver carts came down from Karthwasten last month and only two reached Markarth. The Silver-Bloods say Forsworn. The carters say nothing at all, which is worse.
Somebody left a hagraven feather on the shrine at Old Hroldan. Eydis burned it in the hearth and the smoke went green. Nobody's slept in Tiber Septim's room since.
The Legion pitched a camp near Bthardamz and the Stormcloaks have one above Liar's Retreat. Half a day's walk apart. Any morning now one of them will wake up dead.
Fishermen on the Karth say the river runs red some mornings below Bruca's Leap. Ore runoff, the miners claim. Funny how it only happens after a raid.
The Orcs at Dushnikh Yal are buying every snow fox pelt they can get. Won't say why. My guess is they know something about this winter we don't.
A Dwemer door opened by itself under Markarth last Loredas. Calcelmo had the guards seal the corridor before anyone could see where it went.
Don't take the old road past Dead Crone Rock after dark. The crones up there can sing a man right off a cliff, and they do.
They found a Briarheart dead near Sundered Towers with his chest stitched shut and no heart inside. Even the Forsworn are afraid of whoever did that.
legends: Before the Nords, before the Dwemer, the Reachfolk say the Druadach peaks were the bones of a giant who tried to climb into the sky and was struck down. The hagravens still pick at his ribs, and that is why the stone here bleeds silver.

Faolan, called the Red Eagle, once held every valley from the Karth to the Sea of Ghosts against the Nordic kings. When his last fortress fell he gave his heart to the crones and rose again to fight one more summer. The Reachfolk say he did not die in that last battle. He only lay down to wait for a better one.

The Dwemer cut Markarth from the cliff with tools that sang. When the miners of Cidhna strike a seam at night, some swear they hear the old song answer from below, a low humming that stops the moment anyone speaks.

When Hjalti Early-Beard took Old Hroldan, the storm that broke over the walls spoke his name. Every year since, on the anniversary, the shutters of the inn rattle without wind, and a careful listener can hear a soldier's laugh in the empty room upstairs.

songs.title: Silver in the Stone
lines: ~Silver in the stone and blood upon the silver,
~Cidhna takes the strong and gives the city coin.
~Down goes the lamp and down goes the digger,
~Up comes the ore, and none of it is his.
~Sing for the Karth, it carries what we bury,
~Sing for the Reach, it never once forgives.

songs.title: The Crone on the Crag
lines: ~Feathers on her shoulders, ashes in her hair,
~She sings upon the crag and the wind goes still to hear.
~Shepherd, shut your shutter, hunter, bar your door,
~She wants a heart of briar, and she'll take yours if it's near.

markarth.hook: The city of stone and silver, carved by the Dwemer into the cliffs above the Karth. Every coin here is stamped by the Silver-Bloods, and every secret is buried in Cidhna Mine.
markarth.rumour: Mind what you say in Markarth, friend. The walls are Dwarven and the ears are Silver-Blood, and both of them remember everything.

notes.title: Smelter's Weekly Tally
notes.author: Moth gro-Bagol's apprentice
pages:
#Week of the 3rd, Hearthfire, 4E 201
Ingots from Cidhna: 46.
Ingots from Left Hand Mine: 19.
Ingots from Karthwasten (by cart): 31, should be 44. Cart three never arrived. Driver's widow asks for his wages. Thonar says no wages for undelivered ore.

#Week of the 10th
Cidhna: 51. Left Hand: 17, Skaggi complains of spiders in the lower drift.
Kolskeggr: none. Kolskeggr is never anything anymore.
Note to self: when Master asks why the scales read light, do NOT say 'because the Silver-Bloods take a pinch'. Last apprentice said it. Last apprentice is in Cidhna now.

notes.title: Letter Left at the Temple of Dibella
notes.author: Ysgerd of the Lower Market
pages: Lady of Beauty, I know the priestesses read these before you do, so I will be brief for their sake. My husband Ragnar went to work the carts to Karthwasten in Last Seed. The Silver-Blood factor says Forsworn took the cart at Bruca's Leap.

But Ragnar's knife came back to me. A guard sold it in the market, and he would not say where he got it. If the Forsworn took my husband, why does a city guard have his knife? Give me the courage to ask that question louder, Lady, or give me the sense to stop asking it.

karthwasten.hook: A cluster of miners' houses above the Karth, where the silver belongs to whoever is strongest this season. Lately that has been the Silver-Bloods' sellswords, and the miners are counting the days.
karthwasten.rumour: Karthwasten? Good silver, bad neighbours. The Forsworn on one side, Silver-Blood thugs on the other, and the miners stuck in the middle with their picks.

notes.title: Petition to Jarl Igmund (Unsent)
notes.author: The miners of Karthwasten
pages:
To the Jarl of the Reach, in Understone Keep.
We the undersigned miners of Karthwasten ask for three things. One: a patrol on the road to Markarth, because the Forsworn of Broken Tower Redoubt have taken four of us since the thaw. Two: that the Silver-Bloods' hirelings stop 'inspecting' our ore and keeping a share for the trouble.

Three: that someone, anyone, ask after Bergljot's brother Hrofi, who was dragged off toward Broken Tower on the 9th of Sun's Height. He is alive. The Forsworn shout his name from the ridge to mock us.
Signed with marks, eleven of them. Fjola says we shouldn't send it. Fjola says the last petition got a man killed.

notes.title: Assayer's Slip
pages:
Ore, Karthwasten main shaft. Grade: good. Fair price per ingot at Markarth smelter: 25 septims.
Price offered by Silver-Blood factor: 9 septims.
Price offered by Silver-Blood factor after miners refused: 9 septims and an explanation of how many accidents can happen to a shaft that loses its timbers.
We sold. Of course we sold.

On the back, pressed hard enough to tear the paper:
The factor's man weighed our ore on his own scales, the ones with the dented pan. Ainar says the dent is worth two ingots in every ten. If anyone ever comes from Understone Keep to ask why Karthwasten is poor, show them this slip and show them the pan.

soljunds_sinkhole.hook: A moonstone mine cut into a sinkhole in the Reach hills. The miners dug too deep once, and they still bar the lowest gallery with oak and iron every night.
soljunds_sinkhole.rumour: The Soljund's Sinkhole moonstone shipment got lifted on the road again. Bandits holed up in Liar's Retreat, if you believe the miners. And I do.

notes.title: Board Nailed by the Lower Gallery
pages:
LOWER GALLERY IS SHUT.
It was shut by Soljund himself and it stays shut. If you hear knocking from the other side, that is not a trapped miner. Our miners all come home at sundown, we count them.
If the count is short, we go to the lower gallery with torches and six men. Never one. Never two. Six.

^Added in a different hand:
Count was short on Tirdas. We went with six. We came back with five, and the bar was on the other side of the door.

notes.title: Moonstone Shipping Manifest
notes.author: Hrefna, mine clerk
pages:
#Shipment of the 14th, Last Seed
Moonstone ore, 30 pieces, bound for the smelter at Markarth by the river road.
Escort: two hired swords from Dragon Bridge.
#Remarks
Cart found overturned near Liar's Retreat. Both escorts gone. No blood. Moonstone gone. Escorts paid in advance, which Pa told me never to do. Next time I listen to Pa.

#Postscript
Asked the Stormcloak patrol on the river road if they saw anything. They said they were 'busy with the war'. One of them had a moonstone pin on his cloak. Raw moonstone, uncut, the kind we dig. I did not ask where he got it. I am a clerk, not a fool.

old_hroldan.hook: A roadside inn on the old route to Markarth, raised on the field where Hjalti Early-Beard won a battle that made him an emperor. The room he slept in is still kept, and some say still occupied.
old_hroldan.rumour: Stay at Old Hroldan if you like, just don't ask for the upstairs room. It's taken, has been for about four hundred years.

notes.title: Old Hroldan Guest Book
pages:
Gaius Ventrus, of Bruma. Slept in the Emperor's room on a dare. Left at midnight. Paid in full, didn't take his boots.
Solvi of Rorikstead. Heard marching. Says it was the Legion on the road. There was no Legion on the road.

Unnamed Breton lady. Asked for the room, stayed three nights, wept the whole time. Said he was kind to her. Would not say who.
Ulfgar the Lamp-Keeper adds: the lamp in that room is to be filled every evening, whether or not a guest takes it. House rule since my grandmother's day. Don't ask me what happens if you forget. Someone forgot once.

notes.title: Verses Carved in the Common Room Beam
pages: ~The Reach held Hroldan, stone on stone,
~And Hjalti came with sword alone.
~The sky took breath, the sky took sides,
~And thunder spoke where the Reachman hides.
^Below, in a later hand: and the Reachmen remember, so keep your purse close when you leave by the west road.

Under the carving, a guest has added in charcoal: The innkeeper says the third line is the truest. The day Hjalti took the village, the clouds came down over the walls and a voice rolled out of them that knocked the Reachmen from the battlements. My grandfather said it was the Greybeards. My grandmother said it was the ale. Both of them were there.

dushnikh_yal.hook: An Orc stronghold in a mountain bowl south of Markarth, built around a smithy and a mine and a code older than Skyrim. Outsiders are tolerated if useful, and remembered if not.
dushnikh_yal.rumour: Dushnikh Yal pays honest coin for honest work. Steal from them once and you'll find out what Malacath does with oathbreakers.

notes.title: Smithy Tally, Kept by the First Wife
pages:
Orichalcum from our own mine: 12 ingots. Good.
Iron traded from Markarth: 20 ingots. Bad iron, Nord iron, full of slag. Bring back the same factor and I take his ear.
Charcoal: low. Send the young ones to the woods past Reachwind Eyrie, not the woods by Arkngthamz. Not after last time.

Murbol wants to go after the grave-robbers at Reachwater Rock who sold him a cursed axe. Chief says it is his own honour to mend. I say Murbol is too proud to ask for help and too stubborn to die. One of those will end first.

notes.title: Words Scratched on the Shrine Stone
pages:
Malacath, keeper of the sworn word, the broken and the scorned.
I do not ask you for mercy. You do not have any to give.
I ask for a strong arm and a long memory, so that I remember every Nord who called us beasts at the Markarth gate, and so that my sons remember it after me.
And if there is a little mercy left over, Furious One, let the snow come late this year. The goats are thin.

mor_khazgur.hook: A hard Orc stronghold in the Druadach foothills, where the chief keeps his own laws and his own debts. Its hunters range as far as the black mouth of Darkfall Cave.
mor_khazgur.rumour: The Mor Khazgur hunters lost one of their own in Darkfall Cave. Orcs don't usually ask outsiders for anything. They're asking now.

notes.title: Hunter's Tally Stick, Transcribed
notes.author: Bashnag gro-Larak
pages:
Seven notches: elk, the north meadow.
Three notches: sabre cat, by the falls. One of them nearly had Durz.
One long cut: Durz went into Darkfall Cave after the wounded bear. I told him a wounded bear in a dark hole is the bear's luck, not ours. He went anyway. That was eleven days ago.
No more notches after that. Bashnag doesn't hunt until his brother comes back, or until he knows what in that cave took him. The chief calls it pride. The chief is right.

salvius_farm.hook: A stubborn Imperial family farm in the shadow of Markarth's walls, growing what it can in rocky soil and feeding the miners of Left Hand Mine.
salvius_farm.rumour: The Salvius girl walks a basket of bread up to Left Hand Mine every morning. Lately she comes back with it still full. Her brother hasn't been eating, or hasn't been there.

notes.title: Salvius Household Accounts
notes.author: Aurelia Salvius
pages:
#Last Seed, 4E 201
Sold to Markarth market: cabbage, 2 crates. Leeks, 1 crate. 34 septims.
Sold to Left Hand Mine kitchen: bread, cheese, 18 septims. Skaggi still owes for Hearthfire last.
Paid: rent to the Silver-Bloods for the lower field, 40 septims. Rent was 25 last year.

Lucan's wages from the mine have stopped. Skaggi says the deep drift was closed after the spiders came up through the old Dwemer cut, and that my brother 'went the wrong way'. He went to fetch his tools, Skaggi. He went to fetch the pick Father gave him.

markarth_stables.hook: The last stop before the gates of Markarth, where carters water their horses and swap stories about the road. Most of the stories this year are about Ragnvald.
markarth_stables.rumour: Ask the stablehand at Markarth Stables about her brother. Then buy her a drink. He went up to Ragnvald for treasure and the treasure kept him.

notes.title: Notice Board by the Trough
pages:
CARRIAGE TO WHITERUN: leaves at dawn, Morndas and Fredas. 20 septims. Driver not responsible for Forsworn.
WANTED: escort for silver wagon to Karthwasten. Pay good. Ask at the Silver-Blood Inn. Do NOT ask what happened to the last escort.
LOST: grey mare, white socks, answers to Hilde. Went north toward Ragnvald on her own. Horses have more sense than men, usually.
Scrawled at the bottom: Has anyone seen Eirik Hollow-Voice? Went to Ragnvald on the 2nd of Hearthfire with two hired diggers. The diggers came back. Ask Dagny at the stable.

deepwood_redoubt.hook: A Forsworn stronghold carved into an old Nord barrow in the northern Reach. The hagravens who rule it take children from the Karth valley, and none have been given back.
deepwood_redoubt.rumour: A woodcutter from Dragon Bridge lost his boy to the Forsworn. They took him up to Deepwood Redoubt. The crones there like them young, they say.

notes.title: Letter Pinned with a Woodsman's Knife
notes.author: Horgeir, woodcutter of Dragon Bridge
pages:
To whoever finds this. I could not get past the second gate. My arm is broken and I can hear them singing below.
My son Toki is ten winters old. He has red hair and a whistle carved like a hawk that he will not stop blowing, gods help him. The Forsworn took him from the timber camp near Dragon Bridge Overlook on the 4th of Hearthfire.

The old one with the feathers looked at him the way a butcher looks at a lamb. Her name, I heard the others call it, is Ungrid. If you are stronger than me, go down. If he is alive, bring him out. If he is not, bring me the whistle so I know.
I'll wait at the mill at Dragon Bridge as long as I live. That may not be long.

notes.title: Stained Hide Scroll
notes.author: Gristle-Mother Ungrid
pages:
The briar wants a young heart, a heart that has not yet been afraid. The Nord child is afraid now, he will not do. Keep him for the pot or the trade, whichever.
Next moon we try the Orc girl from Mor Khazgur's hunting grounds. Orcs are born angry. Anger is near to courage.

Madanach's people at Druadach send word: no more taking near the river roads, the Nords grow bold. Madanach is in a cell in Cidhna and gives orders like a king. I give orders like a mother. We will see whose children grow.

darkfall_cave.hook: A black cleft in the Druadach Mountains that breathes cold air even in summer. Falmer hunt its upper passages, and the Orcs of Mor Khazgur say something far older waits at the bottom.
darkfall_cave.rumour: Darkfall Cave goes down further than any map. Orc hunter went in after a wounded bear and nobody's seen him since. Bear neither.

notes.title: Marks Scratched in Charcoal on a Rock
notes.author: Durz gro-Larak
pages:
Bear went left. Blood on the left. I follow.
Pale ones here. Many. They do not see, they listen. Walk on moss, not stone.
Bear dead. Something else ate it first. The pale ones took the meat and they took my bow.

Hiding. Leg bad. If Bashnag comes, brother, my tusk-string is around my neck still. Take it back to the stronghold so they hang it by the fire and not on some pale one's wall.
The wind blows up from below, warm. Warm. In this cold. What is down there?

notes.title: Strips of Hide Knotted in Patterns
pages:
These knotted hide strips were found on a crude altar of chaurus shell. A scholar of Markarth might read them. To the untrained eye they show a crude circle of figures with long ears bowing to a larger figure, and below them a sun, crossed out with a slash of dried blood.
Tied to the bottom is a scrap of Nord cloth, red, the kind the Orcs of Mor Khazgur trade for at Markarth.

Beside the altar, half-buried in guano, a broken Orcish arrow with red fletching lies pointed toward a passage that slopes steeply downward. The air from that passage is warm, and smells faintly of grass, which is impossible this far under the mountain. Someone has scratched a tusk-mark into the stone above it.

dragon_bridge_overlook.hook: A bandit camp on the cliffs above the road south of Dragon Bridge. Its occupants call it a toll house, and the carters who pay call it something else.
dragon_bridge_overlook.rumour: Pay the toll at the Overlook or lose the cart, that's the rule on the north road now. Hrodvar's lot took the whole Karthwasten payroll last week.

notes.title: Toll Ledger
notes.author: Hrodvar Toll-Taker
pages:
#Hearthfire, 4E 201
Timber wagon from Dragon Bridge: 15 septims and a cask of mead. Paid without fuss. Good folk.
Pilgrim to the Shrine to Peryite: nothing. Sick as a dog, didn't want to touch him.
Silver-Blood wagon: tried to run the road. Did not run the road.

Karthwasten payroll chest: 312 septims, plus the ledger and a letter from the clerk. Keep the chest locked, I mean to ransom the ledger back to the miners. They need it to prove what the Silver-Bloods owe them.
Note to the lads: Legion patrols from the Reach camp have been up the road twice. Next time, we let them pass. We're bandits, not idiots.

notes.title: Lookout Duty Roster
pages:
Morndas: Snorri on the ledge, Kjeld at the fire.
Tirdas: Kjeld on the ledge, Snorri at the fire. Snorri, if I find you asleep up there again I will roll you off it myself.
From the ledge you can see Chillwind Depths to the south. If anything comes up out of there, any of those pale things, you ring the pan and you run. Do NOT go and look. Asvald went and looked.

Asvald came back two days later without his boots, his sword or most of his wits. He keeps saying the pale ones 'ate the light'. The chief says to give him a ledge of his own, far away from the fire, and to keep him off the wine. We've kept him off the wine. Not sure that's helping.

brucas_leap_redoubt.hook: A Forsworn hideout built around a waterfall on the upper Karth, where the river leaps a cliff and the Reachmen watch every boat and bridge below.
brucas_leap_redoubt.rumour: That waterfall at Bruca's Leap? The Forsworn have a camp in it. You can hear the drums from the river, under the roar.

notes.title: Bark Strip with Tally Marks
pages: Kept by the watcher at the falls, in the Reach tongue scratched with a thorn. Translated loosely: Four Nord boats down the river this moon. One carried silver. The silver went into the water when we struck. Let the river carry Nord silver to the sea. Let the sea choke on it.

Orc hunters passed by the west path, from Mor Khazgur. We did not strike. Orcs bleed and keep coming. The briar is not cheap, it is not to be spent on Orcs.
The Nords build their camp at Liar's Retreat way, blue cloaks. Let them. Blue cloaks or red cloaks, both stole the Reach.

notes.title: Words Cut into a Cage Bar
pages:
If you read this you are in the cage too, or you are the one who opens it. If you are in the cage: do not eat what they bring on the third day. If you are the one who opens it: the key is not on the chief, he is too clever. It is under the drum.
Gunnar of Karthwasten. Here since Second Seed. Still here.

Below that, a second hand, older and shakier:
Gunnar is gone. They took him on the third day. I did not eat what they brought. I am still here. The drum is by the falls, and the falls are loud enough to cover the sound of a key turning. If I get out I am going home to Karthwasten and never coming back past the river.

deep_folk_crossing.hook: A Dwemer bridge of bronze and stone spanning a gorge in the northern Reach. It has not rusted in four thousand years, and the hum in its pillars has never stopped.
deep_folk_crossing.rumour: Put your ear to the pillars at Deep Folk Crossing and you'll hear it humming. My uncle swore it hummed louder the night before the Markarth Incident.

notes.title: Field Notes on the Crossing
notes.author: Ancilia Varro, of the Markarth Dwemer studies
pages: The pillar glyphs at this crossing are not decoration, whatever my esteemed colleague in Understone Keep says. They are a route marker. Note the repeated sigil of three arcs, which I have also seen at the gates of Bthardamz, to the south.

Note the second sigil, which appears ONLY here and at Bthardamz: a closed eye. My working translation is 'the deep that listens'. I have sent my assistant Fennick to Bthardamz to copy the gate in full. He promised me ten days. It has been twenty.
(Footnote: if anyone finds a lanky Breton with ink on his face and a Dwemer lexicon he swore he'd return, please send him to me in Markarth.)

druadach_redoubt.hook: A cave in the Druadach range that has sheltered Reachmen since before the Nords had a word for them. Its fires are where the Forsworn come to mend, mourn and plan.
druadach_redoubt.rumour: Druadach Redoubt is the Forsworn's home hearth. Every Briarheart that ever raided a farm went there to have his wounds sewn up.

notes.title: Healer's Tally on Birch Bark
pages:
Brought in from the raid at the Karthwasten road: three. Arrow in the thigh, axe in the shoulder, one who will not wake.
From Broken Tower: one, Nord sword cut. He laughs about it. Let him laugh, it is good for the blood.
Needed from the woods: snowberries, nightshade for the one who will not wake, if he does not wake by the moon's end.
To any Reachman who reads: Druadach is not for war. Do not bring the hearts of Nords to these fires. Bring them to Deepwood and to the crones, who want such things. Here we keep only our own alive.

cliffside_retreat.hook: A lonely cabin perched on the cliffs east of the Karth gorge, with a cellar dug deeper than any honest hermit needs.
cliffside_retreat.rumour: Old cabin up on the cliff by Liar's Retreat. Hermit who lived there never came to market, but he always had coin. Makes you wonder where from.

notes.title: Hermit's Diary
notes.author: Ottmar the Cliff-Dweller
pages:
#2nd of Rain's Hand
The goats have found the path down to the river again. Fetched them back. Saw smoke from Liar's Retreat. Bandits, or the Stormcloaks' new camp. Neither one buys goat cheese.

#9th of Rain's Hand
Dug the cellar deeper. The rock gives way to old worked stone, carved by someone, not Dwemer, not Nord. Found a little iron key in a niche, no lock to fit it.

#20th of Rain's Hand
Strange men came asking for the key. Robes under their cloaks, red as fresh meat. I said I had no key. They said they'd come back. I believe them. Buried the key where the goats won't dig.

harmugstahl.hook: A ruined Nordic fort east of the Druadach peaks, taken over by a solitary mage. Travellers who take shelter there are not seen again, and the spiders have grown very large.
harmugstahl.rumour: Some wizard's holed up in Harmugstahl breeding spiders. Big as a cart. I'm not saying the man is mad. I'm saying I'm not going to check.

notes.title: Observations on Arachnid Vigour
notes.author: Ostrel Vane, formerly of the College of Winterhold
pages: Day 61. Specimen IV (the large female) has consumed the Karthwasten shepherd entirely. Growth after feeding: a third of a hand-span along the leg. Remarkable. The College would never fund this, which is why the College will never know.

Day 64. The binding glyph holds the specimens docile only within the walls of Harmugstahl. When I tried to walk Specimen IV to Dragontooth Crater to test the effect of dragon presence, she turned on me, and I lost two fingers and a good cloak.
Day 70. Visitors expected. Some sellsword the miners sent. I shall extend my hospitality. Specimen IV has not eaten in four days.

notes.title: Crumpled Note in a Satchel
notes.author: Teit, shepherd of Karthwasten
pages:
Teit of Karthwasten, if anyone asks. The mage said he would pay for sheep and pay well. I brought him six. He paid in gold, then asked if I would like to see what the sheep were for.
I am writing this in the room he locked me in. I can hear them moving in the walls. If you find this, the mage is called Vane. He wears a College ring on a hand with two fingers missing. Stop him. Please tell my wife at Karthwasten I did not run off. Tell her I was a fool, but I did not run off.

liars_retreat.hook: A river cave on the Karth where a smooth-talking bandit keeps his crew and his stolen moonstone. Half the stories he tells are lies. The other half are worse.
liars_retreat.rumour: Sweet-Tongue Ottar runs Liar's Retreat. He'll sell you a treasure map, a horse, his own mother. Not one of them's real.

notes.title: A Very Convincing Treasure Map
notes.author: Sweet-Tongue Ottar
pages:
Copy number nine. Sold for 40 septims each to eight fools so far.
The map shows Four Skull Lookout, south of Karthwasten, with an X by the skull that faces west and the words 'Dig beneath the sunset skull, a Legion paymaster's chest, lost 4E 176'.

In smaller writing on the back, in Ottar's own hand, not meant for buyers:
The joke is, I made it up from a story my old captain told me, and the captain swore it was true. Never dug there myself. Never wanted to know. A man who digs up his own lie has nothing left to sell.

notes.title: Orders for the Crew
notes.author: Ottar
pages: Lads. The moonstone from Soljund's Sinkhole stays in the strongbox till the fence from Markarth comes. Nobody touches it. Nobody tells the Stormcloaks next door about it either. They'd call it 'requisitioning' and give us a speech about Talos.

If the Soljund's folk send someone, tell them the cart went into the river. Weep a little if you can. Gjuki, you're good at weeping, do the weeping.
The escorts we took are in the back cave, eating our food. Ransom them or let them go, I don't care, but stop feeding them the good cheese.

reach_stormcloak_camp.hook: A Stormcloak war camp pitched on a ridge in the middle Reach, close enough to Markarth to make the Jarl nervous and close enough to the Forsworn to make the soldiers jumpy.
reach_stormcloak_camp.rumour: There's a Stormcloak camp up past Karthwasten. The men in it remember the Markarth Incident and they're itching to see the Reach under Ulfric again.

notes.title: Standing Orders, Reach Camp
notes.author: Ice-Veins Gunnolf, Stormcloak Captain
pages:
1. No soldier leaves the camp alone. The Forsworn in Broken Tower Redoubt have taken two sentries this month.
2. The Imperial camp is at the foot of the hills by Bthardamz. You are not to engage it without orders. We are here to watch, not to start a war we can't finish from a tent.

3. Any dispatch rider seen on the Deep Folk Crossing road is to be stopped and searched. The Legion moves its letters that way.
4. The bandits in Liar's Retreat are not our allies, whatever they say. Sweet-Tongue offered me moonstone for safe passage. I said yes. Now none of you will touch it until I say so.
5. Talos guide us. Shine your boots.

notes.title: Letter Home, Never Sent
notes.author: Hroar, Stormcloak soldier
pages:
Mother,
We are camped in the Reach. It is not like Windhelm. The rocks here are red and the people look at you as if you owe them something. Maybe we do. Old Varmund says when Ulfric took Markarth back from the Forsworn, the streets ran so red you could not tell blood from the stone.
I do not tell Varmund that I don't think that's a thing to be proud of. Bake Inga a honey cake for me. I'll be home by Evening Star, or I won't.

dragontooth_crater.hook: A crater blasted into the Reach highlands, its rim jagged like a broken jaw. A dragon has made its lair on the scorched stone, and the hunters of Karthwasten no longer go north.
dragontooth_crater.rumour: There's a dragon roosting at Dragontooth Crater, plain as day. Comes down on the Karthwasten goats every few days. Somebody ought to do something, and by somebody I mean not me.

notes.title: Scorched Hunter's Journal
notes.author: Ingrith Sure-Shot
pages:
#14th of Frostfall
Watched it from the rim all morning. Grey-green scales, a notch out of the left wing. It sleeps in the middle of the crater with its head toward Harmugstahl. The miners at Karthwasten call it the Goat-Thief. The Greybeards would call it something else, I suppose.

#15th of Frostfall
Went closer. It woke. It spoke. I do not know the words but I felt them in my teeth, like the hum at Deep Folk Crossing. Burned my bow arm. I'm writing this left-handed.

#16th of Frostfall
I cannot climb the rim with this arm. If you read this, kill it. Aim under the jaw, where the scales are thin. I put an arrow there before it burned me and it bled.

bthardamz.hook: A sprawling Dwemer ruin in the northwest Reach, whose halls echo with the hiss of steam and the clatter of machines still guarding their makers' secrets.
bthardamz.rumour: Some Breton scholar's assistant went into Bthardamz with a lexicon and never came out. His mistress in Markarth is offering good coin for the book. Not so much for the Breton.

notes.title: Fennick's Copying Journal
notes.author: Fennick Aulus, assistant to Ancilia Varro
pages:
#Day 1
Mistress says copy the gate glyphs and come back. Easy. Copied the gate in a morning. But the door was open. Who leaves a Dwemer door open? Nobody leaves a Dwemer door open. I'll just look.

#Day 3
The spiders don't notice me if I stay still and hum. Discovered this by accident. The Lexicon fits the slot by the great hall door perfectly, which is surely meaningful.

#Day 6
The big one woke when the Lexicon turned in the slot. Steam everywhere. I've hidden in a pipe room with no food and a very sore ankle. The Lexicon is still in the slot by the great hall. Mistress will kill me. If the centurion doesn't first.

notes.title: Words Daubed on a Bronze Panel
pages:
Written in something that is not quite paint:
THE TASKMASTER SEES THE ORDER IN THE MACHINE. THE DEEP FOLK SERVED NO ONE, SO THEY WERE ERASED. WE SERVE. WE ARE NOT ERASED. ROT IS ORDER. ROT IS ORDER.
Below it, small and frantic: Whoever wrote that came past my hiding place three times. They smell like a sickroom. I don't think they're scholars. F.

And under that, scratched with a stylus in a neat scholar's hand: Third pass today. One of them stopped by my pipe and sniffed, then walked on. Either they cannot smell a living man over their own sickness, or the Taskmaster's servants have no orders concerning lanky Bretons. I shall try not to give them any reason to write some.

broken_tower_redoubt.hook: A shattered Nordic fort in the middle Reach, its broken tower crowned with Forsworn totems. The Briarheart who rules it keeps Nord captives, and the miners of Karthwasten hear their names shouted from the walls.
broken_tower_redoubt.rumour: The Forsworn at Broken Tower Redoubt took Bergljot's brother. They yell his name from the ridge at night just to watch Karthwasten flinch.

notes.title: Carving on the Chieftain's Seat
pages:
Cut deep into the wood with a stone knife, in rough Tamrielic so that Nord captives can read it:
THIS TOWER WAS REACH BEFORE IT WAS NORD. IT WILL BE REACH AFTER.
KAELIN THORN-CHEST SITS HERE. HIS HEART IS IN A HAGRAVEN'S JAR AT DEEPWOOD. KILL HIM AND HE STANDS UP AGAIN, ASK THE NORDS WHO TRIED.

Below, in charcoal, in a different and shakier hand:
I tried. He stood up again. But he was slower the second time. Aim for the briar. - H.

notes.title: Folded Letter Under a Fur
notes.author: Hrofi of Karthwasten
pages: Bergljot, if this ever reaches you. I am not a prisoner anymore, not the way you think. The Reachwoman who brought me water when I was in the cage is called Mairi. Her father died in Cidhna for a theft the Silver-Bloods made up.

I have seen what they are fighting for, and I have seen what we dig for, and I know who gets fat on it. I am not coming back to swing a pick for Thonar Silver-Blood's coin purse. Tell Mother I am alive. Tell her I am sorry. Do not send anyone. I mean it, sister. Do not send anyone.

shrine_to_peryite.hook: A Daedric shrine in a misty glade west of Karthwasten, where the sick and the desperate pray to Peryite, Taskmaster of the lowest Oblivion, for a cure or a curse.
shrine_to_peryite.rumour: Folk with the rattles go to the Shrine to Peryite to pray. Some come back cured. Some come back worse. Most don't come back at all.

notes.title: Prayer Pinned with a Bone Needle
pages: Taskmaster, you who keep the order of the rot. My boy has the brain rot and the healers at the Temple of Dibella want silver I do not have. The priests of Arkay say pray. I prayed. He got worse.

So I pray to you now, Lord of Pestilence, because you are the only god in the Reach who admits what sickness is. Take it from him. Put it in me if you must. I am old, the boy is not.
The sick ones who camp by the shrine tell me you never give without a price. Fine. Name it.
- Fjola of Karthwasten

notes.title: Names on a Strip of Linen
pages:
Those who went to Bthardamz to serve the Taskmaster:
Orchendor? No - he LEADS. He does not go, he sends.
Kjar of Dragon Bridge. Hilda the Pale. Two Bretons from Markarth who would not give names. Askar, who was a guard in Understone Keep until his skin went grey.
Those who stay at the shrine: me. I am still deciding. When the pustules reach my eyes I will go too. They say in Bthardamz the pain becomes a kind of song.

reach_imperial_camp.hook: A Legion war camp at the foot of the hills below Bthardamz, holding the Reach for the Empire and for Jarl Igmund. Its couriers ride out every week, and lately not all of them ride back.
reach_imperial_camp.rumour: The Legion lost a dispatch rider on the Deep Folk Crossing road. The legate's fuming. Wants to know if it was the Forsworn or the bearded ones from Windhelm.

notes.title: Report to Castle Dour
notes.author: Tribune Calvius Arro, Reach Camp
pages:
To the General's office, Castle Dour, Solitude.
Sir, I regret to report that dispatch rider Quintus Asellio did not arrive at Dragon Bridge on schedule. His horse returned without him on the 11th of Frostfall, with a Forsworn arrow in the saddle.

I do not accept the obvious answer. The Stormcloak camp near Liar's Retreat has openly boasted of stopping riders on that road, and a Forsworn arrow is easy enough to buy in Karthwasten. Asellio carried the troop rolls for the whole Reach garrison. If they fell into Ulfric's hands, every patrol from Markarth to Bthardamz is compromised.
I request permission to send a party to Deep Folk Crossing to recover the satchel. Failing permission, I intend to hire someone and not ask.

notes.title: Quartermaster's Shortages
pages:
Arrows: low. Request sent to Markarth. Request ignored by Markarth.
Bandages: low, owing to the Forsworn.
Wine: none, owing to the soldiers.
Morale: see Wine.
Note for the tribune: the men will not stand watch facing the Dragon Burial Mound to the south. They say it moves at night. I have explained that mounds do not move. They have explained that I do not stand watch.

Further requests, unanswered:
One (1) priest of Arkay, for the men's nerves and the dead's sake.
One (1) map of the Bthardamz approaches that does not end in the words 'here be machines'.
Rope: plenty. We have so much rope. Nobody knows why. Do not let the men near the rope after the wine runs out.

sundered_towers.hook: Twin broken towers on a ridge above the Karth, held by a Forsworn band that is far too well armed for raiders who live on roots and stolen goats.
sundered_towers.rumour: Funny thing about the Sundered Towers Forsworn. Steel arrowheads, new bowstrings, Markarth-forged knives. Somebody in the city is selling. Somebody in the city is getting rich.

notes.title: A Second Ledger, Hidden in a Boot
notes.author: Vorald, Silver-Blood factor
pages:
#Kept separately from the Silver-Blood books
Sun's Dawn: 40 steel arrowheads to the Towers. Received in kind: one silver cart from the Karthwasten road, contents to be 'recovered' by me and returned to the Silver-Bloods at a finder's fee.
First Seed: 12 steel knives. Received: the Karthwasten payroll, likewise recovered.

So the Forsworn get steel, the miners get robbed, and I get a reward for finding what I paid to have stolen. Thonar must never see this book. He would not object to the scheme. He would object that I did not cut him in.
Note: Nairne the Stone-Singer is getting greedy. Bring her a hagraven feather cloak from Markarth next time, she likes those.

notes.title: Song Scratched in Red Ochre
pages: ~The Nord sells steel to kill the Nord,
~And we take it, and we laugh.
~He thinks the Reach is bought with knives,
~The Reach is bought with blood, and half.
^Translated from the Reach tongue by a guard of Markarth, who added: 'Half of what? Never found out. Ask them.'

The same guard's report continues: The Forsworn at the Towers sang this as they drove the Karthwasten silver wagon off the road. I lay in the ditch and heard every word. When they were gone I found the wagon's strongbox already opened with a key, not broken. Forsworn don't carry keys. Somebody gave them one.

ragnvald.hook: An ancient Nordic ruin in the hills north of Markarth, built around a sunken courtyard where the dead keep watch. Treasure hunters go there in pairs, and come back in ones.
ragnvald.rumour: Ragnvald's an old Nord tomb up north of Markarth. Eirik Hollow-Voice went there for gold. His sister's still waiting at the stables.

notes.title: Treasure Hunter's Journal
notes.author: Eirik Hollow-Voice
pages:
#2nd of Hearthfire
Arrived with Brand and Olaf, hired at the Silver-Blood Inn. The courtyard is real, just as Grandfather drew it. Draugr asleep in the walls. We tiptoe like thieves in a nursery.

#3rd of Hearthfire
The tithe-chamber. Silver plate, a whole wall of it, offerings to the barrow's master. Brand and Olaf filled their packs and left me in the dark. Cowards. I still have the lantern.

#4th of Hearthfire
The master woke. Hrodulf, it says on his coffin. Tithe-Keeper. He wants the silver back, every piece, and I am the only one left to pay. I am hiding behind his throne. Dagny, if this reaches you, I'm sorry about the mare.

notes.title: Words Carved Around the Tithe Wall
pages:
Rendered by a scholar's rough hand from the old Nordic runes:
Here Hrodulf keeps the tithe of the valley. What the living gave, the dead hold. Whoever takes from the wall pays from the blood.
And beneath, the scholar adds: The runes for 'valley' here are those used for the lands of the Karth before the Reachmen drove the first Nords out. This barrow is older than Markarth's Nord kings. Treat it with respect, or with a very large axe.

blind_cliff_cave.hook: A cave in the cliffs south of Karthwasten, where the hagravens of the Reach perform their darkest rite: turning a living woman into one of their own.
blind_cliff_cave.rumour: Blind Cliff Cave belongs to the crones. They take Reachwomen in there and what comes out has feathers. Don't you look at me like that, it's true.

notes.title: Message Woven into a Hair Ribbon
notes.author: Aiwen of the Karth
pages: My mother sold me to Ulvra Ash-Tongue for a briar. She thinks it is an honour. On the dark of the moon they will do the becoming and I will not be Aiwen anymore.

I have woven this into my ribbon and thrown it out the smoke hole. If the wind is kind, someone will find it near the Lover Stone, where my Nord boy used to wait for me. Tell him not to come. Tell anyone else to come with fire. The crone keeps the rite-knife on her belt. Without it there is no becoming.

notes.title: Bone Tablet of the Becoming
notes.author: Ulvra Ash-Tongue
pages:
The ash from a willing heart. The feather from an old mother. The knife that was bathed in the Karth when the moon was drowned.
She must not be willing in the mouth. She must be willing in the blood. The girl Aiwen is unwilling in the mouth and that is better, her anger feeds the feathers.
After the becoming, take her to Dead Crone Rock to learn the songs. The sisters there will teach her to sing a Nord off a cliff.

rebels_cairn.hook: A barrow raised over Faolan the Red Eagle, the Reach king who would not kneel. The Forsworn guard it as a holy place, and now someone else is digging.
rebels_cairn.rumour: They say Red Eagle sleeps in Rebel's Cairn with his sword on his chest. Lately someone with a shovel and a lot of candles has been poking around up there.

notes.title: Excavation Notes
notes.author: Corvin Ashdown
pages: The Red Eagle's bones are not ordinary bones. A man who gave his heart to the hagravens and still walked keeps the habit of walking. With the right working he will walk for me.

The Forsworn who come to pray are a nuisance. Killed two. Raised one. He is a poor servant, keeps trying to kneel at the tomb.
The Eagle's sword is not here, which annoys me. The Forsworn at Red Eagle Redoubt have it, I suspect. No matter. I want the king, not his cutlery. One more night of chanting and the seal on the inner chamber breaks.

notes.title: Lament on a Cairn Stone
pages:
Chipped into a standing stone at the entrance, in the Reach tongue, with a Nord's translation chalked beneath:
~Here lies the Eagle, who would not bow.

~He gave his heart for one more spring.
~The spring came. The Eagle fell.
~Wake him, and he will fight again. Let him sleep, and he will dream us free.

Beneath the lament, painted fresh in ochre: The pale man with candles came last night. He spat on the Eagle's stone and called it a rock. Three of us went to drive him off. One came back, and that one now walks the cairn with empty eyes and kneels to nobody. Briarhearts of Red Eagle Redoubt, if you hear this, come.

four_skull_lookout.hook: A crumbling Nordic watchpost south of Karthwasten, marked by four stone skulls that stare out over the Reach. Treasure maps to it are sold cheap in every inn west of Whiterun.
four_skull_lookout.rumour: Bought a map to Four Skull Lookout from a smooth-talking fellow by the river. Forty septims. Wife says it's fake. Wife is usually right. Still, though.

notes.title: Message Chalked on a Skull
pages:
To the next fool with Ottar's map: I dug under the east skull, the north skull and the south skull. Nothing but roots and a dead skeever. I am too tired and too angry to do the west one. Liar's Retreat earned its name.
- Arngrim of Dragon Bridge, out forty septims and a good shovel
Beneath, in another hand: The draugr in here don't care about maps, by the way. Bring something sharp. - B.

And beneath both, in a third hand, very small: It is always the last place you'd look, isn't it. West skull. I would have dug it myself but I heard the draugr wake and I am not paid enough. Nobody is paid enough for draugr.

notes.title: Legion Paymaster's Note (Water-Stained)
notes.author: Paymaster Avidius Crell
pages:
4E 176. The city has fallen back to Ulfric's militia and the Forsworn are scattering into the hills. I am not taking the cohort's pay chest down to Markarth through that. Buried it under the skull that faces the sunset, at the old lookout. Will return for it with an escort.
If I do not return, the gold belongs to the Emperor. Which is to say it belongs to whoever is first with a spade.

Second page, the ink badly run:
The chest holds the cohort's pay, an officer's sword, and my own savings, eleven years of them. If my wife in Bruma ever reads this, I am sorry. I told you the Reach would be quiet. I told you the Nords and the Reachmen had made their peace. I was wrong about everything, my love, except you.

dustmans_cairn.hook: A Nordic barrow on the plains west of Whiterun, near Hamvir's Rest. Its draugr guard a fragment of an old and famous blade, and armed strangers have been seen going down its steps.
dustmans_cairn.rumour: Dustman's Cairn? Bad place. Lately men in silver-trimmed armour have been seen going in. Werewolf hunters, my brother says. Hunting what, in a tomb?

notes.title: Surveyor's Notes for the Jarl of Whiterun
notes.author: Hallvard Stone-Counter, surveyor
pages: Dustman's Cairn lies on the old boundary between Whiterun Hold and the Reach, which means both Jarls claim it and neither wants to pay to have it guarded. Entrance faces east. Steps descend steeply. Air smells of grave-dust and, oddly, fresh wolf.

Saw armed men in mismatched steel enter at dusk. They wore silver hand badges. When I asked their business, the tall one said, 'Hunting dogs.' I do not keep dogs, and I left.
Recommend the barrow be marked on hold maps as dangerous and left well alone, by order of both Jarls, which they will never agree on.

notes.title: Scrap from Hamvir's Rest
pages:
Brother,
The ones from the cairn came to Hamvir's Rest again asking for a guide. I told them I know nothing of the cairn. They paid me anyway and asked what the Companions of Whiterun look like, how many there are, where they drink. I told them the Bannered Mare. Maybe I shouldn't have.
The stew is still bad here. The view is still good. Come visit when the roads are safe, which is never.

Postscript: Last night one of them came back from the cairn alone and bleeding, shouting about a wolf that walked on two legs and wore a woman's face. His friends hushed him and paid for the room in silver. I've hidden the silver under the floor. It feels like the kind of coin somebody comes back for.

red_eagle_redoubt.hook: A Forsworn stronghold in the hills by Karthspire, named for the Red Eagle and fiercely held by those who keep his memory. His sword is said to lie somewhere in its depths.
red_eagle_redoubt.rumour: Red Eagle Redoubt is where the Forsworn keep their pride. And their old king's sword, if the songs are right. Nobody's been in to check and come out.

notes.title: Oath Carved Above the Inner Door
pages:
Carved in the Reach tongue and painted with ochre, renewed every spring:
WE ARE THE EAGLE'S FEATHERS. WE GUARD HIS TALON. WHOEVER TAKES IT WITHOUT HIS BLESSING TAKES IT FROM OUR HANDS AND OUR HANDS DO NOT OPEN.
Below, newer: Rebel's Cairn is disturbed. A pale man with candles. Send three Briarhearts. Send all.

And under that, a third carving, crude and furious:
The pale man has been driven off for now. Two Briarhearts dead. The cairn's seal holds. Whoever comes to this door with Nord steel and no blessing, know that the Eagle's feathers do not forgive. Know also that we are tired, and that tired men fight harder.

notes.title: Scout's Report to Understone Keep
notes.author: Faleen's runner
pages:
Counted fifteen Forsworn at Red Eagle Redoubt, including two Briarhearts and one crone. They go out by the south path to Karthspire Camp and to the river at Soljund's Sinkhole.
Their chief speaks of an old sword as if it were a living king. The men treat the inner chamber as a shrine. Recommend we leave it alone until we have the men. Recommend we never have the men.

Added at the bottom in the steward's hand: The Jarl agrees. Red Eagle Redoubt is to be marked on the maps and avoided. Any adventurer who wishes to try it may do so at their own expense and with their own life. The Jarl regrets in advance. The Jarl does not offer a refund.

bleakwind_bluff.hook: A windswept rise crowned with a Forsworn tower, where a hagraven keeps a garden of thorns and a cage full of what she calls guests.
bleakwind_bluff.rumour: Wind never stops on Bleakwind Bluff. You'd think that'd blow the stink of the crone's pot away. It doesn't.

notes.title: The Crone's Guest List
pages:
Scratched on hide with a burnt twig:
The Rorikstead peddler. Soft. For the pot.
The Orc from Dushnikh Yal. Hard. For the briar.
The Nord girl with the moonstone ring from Soljund's Sinkhole. Pretty. For the trade to Blind Cliff Cave.
The old man from Lund's Hut. Stringy. Let him go, nobody wants him.
Under the list: Lund's man went home and told the others. Good. Let them know the bluff is ours. Let them be afraid on the road to Rorikstead.

kolskeggr_mine.hook: A gold mine in the hills east of Markarth that once fed half the Reach. The miners have been driven out by Forsworn, and the gold sits in the dark with no one to dig it.
kolskeggr_mine.rumour: Kolskeggr Mine used to keep Markarth in gold. Now the Forsworn have it, and the only one who still goes near is an Imperial named Pavo who won't give up his claim.

notes.title: Last Shift Roster
pages:
#Kolskeggr Mine, 4E 201
Morning shift: Olfrid, Hrogar, Ennis, Rolf. Afternoon shift: Ulfr, Thane's boy, Margret.
Night shift: none since the Forsworn came down from the Lover Stone path.
Pay for the month: withheld by the Silver-Blood factor until the mine produces again. The mine cannot produce while the Forsworn hold it. The factor says that is our problem.

Scratched beside the roster with a nail: Pavo Attius, the Imperial who holds the claim now, came to tell us the Forsworn would be gone by spring. That was two springs ago. Ennis says he'd sooner swing a pick for the Forsworn than wait for the Silver-Bloods to pay us. Ennis says a lot of things after dark.

notes.title: Prospector's Sketch
notes.author: Ennis the Prospector
pages:
The richest seam runs east, toward Sky Haven way, but the old Dwemer workings cut across it. Our picks broke into a Dwemer tunnel last winter. Warm air came out, and the smell of oil.
I marked the spot with a red cross on the wall and the foreman bricked it over. Every miner in Kolskeggr knows where the red cross is. Not one of us will tell the Silver-Bloods, because they'd send us back in.

Second page, folded small:
If the Silver-Bloods ever get hold of this mine for good, they'll break that wall in a day and send us down the Dwemer tunnel with a lamp and no wages. I'd rather it stayed in Forsworn hands than theirs. Don't tell anyone I said that. Especially not in Markarth.

karthspire_camp.hook: A Forsworn camp on the trail up the Karthspire, where sentries watch the bridge and the valley below with arrows nocked and ears open.
karthspire_camp.rumour: There's a Forsworn camp guarding the way up Karthspire. Why they'd guard a rock nobody wants is anyone's guess.

notes.title: Sentry Orders on Bark
pages: Watch the bridge. Watch the valley. If Nords come in twos, shoot them. If Nords come in tens, run to the spire and warn the others. If someone comes alone and knows the old path behind the falls, do not shoot them. Follow them. Find out what they know.

The crones say there is a door in the spire that the Nords' ancestors made. A door with a dragon's face. It does not open for Reachmen. It does not open for hagravens. It waits for someone. We watch for that someone too.

karthspire.hook: A towering crag above the Karth valley, held by Forsworn and wrapped in mist. Old soldiers' tales speak of a hidden temple of the Blades in the cliffs behind it.
karthspire.rumour: Karthspire's crawling with Forsworn. My grandfather used to say the Blades built something up there in the old days, before the Thalmor ran them all down.

notes.title: Fragment of an Old Blades Chronicle
pages: ...and so in the reign of Reman the Dragonguard raised a sanctuary in the Reach, behind the spire that the Reachmen call Karth's Tooth. Its door bore the face of a dragon and would open only to blood of a certain kind, the old Dragonguard being much concerned with such things.

Within, on a great wall, the Akaviri carved what they had learned of the end of days, so that those who came after would know the shape of it. The chronicler does not record whether any of them understood the carving. Only that they spoke of it in low voices, and that the Grandmaster took his meals facing the other way.

left_hand_mine.hook: A silver mine just outside Markarth's walls, worked by free miners who sell to the Silver-Bloods. Its deepest drift broke into an old Dwemer cut, and something cold came up through the gap.
left_hand_mine.rumour: Left Hand Mine shut its deep drift last month. Spiders, says Skaggi. Big ones, from the old Dwarven tunnels. The Salvius boy was down there when they closed it.

notes.title: Notice Nailed at the Drift Mouth
notes.author: Skaggi Scar-Face
pages:
DEEP DRIFT IS CLOSED.
Frostbite spiders came through the Dwarven cut. Two men bitten, one dead. No mining past the second timber frame until the Jarl sends guards or the spiders get bored.
The Jarl will not send guards. Spiders do not get bored.

To whoever took Lucan Salvius's pick from the rack: it was not on the rack. He went back down for it after we closed the drift. I told him not to. He's an Imperial. They never listen, they just quote laws at you.

notes.title: Letters Scraped into a Timber
notes.author: Lucan Salvius
pages:
Scratched with a knife on a pit prop deep in the closed drift:
LUCAN WAS HERE. FOUND THE PICK. SPIDERS BETWEEN ME AND THE LIGHT. GOING THROUGH THE DWARF DOOR TO FIND ANOTHER WAY OUT.
IF I AM NOT HOME BY THE MARKET DAY TELL AURELIA THE PICK IS FATHER'S AND SHE MUST HAVE IT. I AM NOT LEAVING IT TO A SPIDER.

Scratched further along the same timber, fainter, as if by a tired hand:
DWARF DOOR LEADS DOWN NOT UP. COLD. WEBS. SOMETHING BIG HAS ITS NEST BY THE STEAM PIPE. I HAVE THE PICK. I AM GOING TO SIT VERY STILL UNTIL IT SLEEPS. AURELIA, THE SPICED BREAD WAS GOOD. SAVE ME SOME.

reachwater_rock.hook: An ancient tomb hidden in the cliffs where the Reach's waters spill from the rock. Grave robbers use its outer halls as a hideout and have not yet learned to fear the inner ones.
reachwater_rock.rumour: The diggers in Reachwater Rock robbed an Orc stronghold and sold the loot in Markarth. Bold. Stupid, but bold. The Orcs want their axe back.

notes.title: Grave Robbers' Shares
notes.author: Fjotra the Spade
pages:
Share-out, 20th of Last Seed:
Silver urn from the outer hall: sold in Markarth, 60 septims, split five ways.
Draugr rings: 4, sold, 30 septims. Kalf wants his own share for doing the prising. Kalf gets a fist.
Orichalcum axe, from the Orc stronghold at Dushnikh Yal (the night raid): NOT sold. Nobody in Markarth will touch it. Orc carvings on the haft, a grudge-mark, they say.
Note to self: the inner door has a puzzle of claws and pillars. Kalf thinks he's worked it out. If he's wrong we lose Kalf. If he's right we get rich. Either way the shares go further.

notes.title: Ward Carved over the Inner Door
pages:
Rendered from the old runes:
Here sleep the oath-keepers of the Reachwater. Water runs from the rock and memory runs from the dead. Drink the one and you will live. Take the other and you will join us.
Below, freshly scratched: Kalf drank from the pool. Kalf's fine. Kalf took a ring off a body. Kalf's not fine.

A third line, scratched hard into the stone beside the door, in the same rough hand:
Kalf woke them. They're all awake now. Fjotra says the Orc axe brought the bad luck and wants to throw it in the pool. I say we sell it back to the Orcs. Fjotra says the Orcs will kill us. I say the draugr will kill us first.

reachcliff_cave.hook: A barrow cut into the cliffs of the southern Reach, home to the hungry dead and, some whisper, to living worshippers with a terrible appetite.
reachcliff_cave.rumour: Something's living in Reachcliff Cave that leaves bones picked clean. Not wolves. Wolves don't use knives.

notes.title: Torn List of the Missing
pages:
Scrawled on the back of a Markarth guard notice:
Orla, beggar, went south toward the cliffs, Sun's Height.
The Bosmer trapper from Dushnikh Yal's road, Last Seed.
Two pilgrims bound for Old Hroldan, Hearthfire.
All seen last on the road past Reachcliff Cave. All with no family worth asking. Whoever's doing this chooses well.
And beneath, in red that is not ink: Not 'whoever'. We are many, and we are always hungry, and our Lady is pleased.

Folded into the list, a second scrap in a shaking hand:
I followed the beggar Orla's tracks to the cave mouth and smelled cooking. Good cooking. Herbs and fat and smoke. I nearly went in. Then I saw the bones stacked by the door, neat as firewood, and every one of them had been scraped clean with a knife. I am going back to Markarth and I am never eating meat again.

reachwind_eyrie.hook: A wind-scoured Nordic watchtower on a crag above Dushnikh Yal's valley, where hawks nest in the broken battlements and old signal fires still smudge the stones.
reachwind_eyrie.rumour: The Orcs of Dushnikh Yal climb up to Reachwind Eyrie to take hawk chicks for training. Brave lot. The wind up there's taken more men than the Forsworn ever did.

notes.title: Signal Code Cut into the Parapet
pages:
A tally of fire-codes carved by the Nord wardens who held this tower in the Second Era:
ONE FIRE: Reachmen on the river.
TWO FIRES: Reachmen in the hills.
THREE FIRES: dragon. (This line has been scratched out, then carved again, then scratched out once more.)

Added later, by an Orc hand, in thick strokes:
No Nord wardens here now. Only Gashna's hawks and the wind. If you come for chicks, leave a strip of meat for the mother. She remembers the ones who don't.

hag_rock_redoubt.hook: A Forsworn camp clustered on a rock in the hills south of Markarth, ruled by a hagraven and fortified with bone and briar. Bards say a thorn-sword lies at its heart.
hag_rock_redoubt.rumour: Hag Rock's not a place you visit, it's a place you get dragged to. The crone there grows a sword out of a briar, they say. Bloodthorn, the songs call it.

notes.title: Scratches on a Drum Frame
pages:
On the frame of a broken Forsworn drum, in the Reach tongue: Beat once for the hunters' return. Beat twice for the briar. Beat thrice for the Nords at the gate.
The crone took the Nord bard's drum as a prize after the raid on the Markarth road. She says its sound is sweet. We say it is a Nord sound and wakes the dead in Dead Crone Rock across the valley.
Below: The crone does not care. She likes waking them.

notes.title: Markarth Bounty Notice
notes.author: Steward of Understone Keep
pages:
By order of Jarl Igmund. A bounty of 200 septims is offered for the hagraven of Hag Rock Redoubt, who has led raids on the stables, the Salvius farm and the road to Purewater Run.
Proof of the deed: her head, or her staff, or failing both, the testimony of two sober witnesses. Sober witnesses have proven hard to find in Markarth this year.

Scrawled across the bottom by some wag at the Silver-Blood Inn: Two sober witnesses can be had at the inn for 10 septims each, sober guaranteed until noon. And beneath, in another hand: The crone's staff is made of a Nord's thighbone. Bring that back and you won't need witnesses. You'll need a priest.

dead_crone_rock.hook: A ruined Nordic fortress on a sheer crag south of Markarth, held by hagravens and their servants. An ancient word wall stands on the heights beside it.
dead_crone_rock.rumour: Climb Dead Crone Rock and the crones up there will sing for you. Last thing you'll ever hear, mind, but very pretty.

notes.title: Song Written in Soot on a Shield
pages: ~Come up, come up, the climb is long,
~And sweeter at the top the song.
~We'll sing your name, we'll sing your bones,
~We'll sing you into the cold stones.
^Found on a Nord shield, the bearer's name scratched off. Someone took the trouble to scratch it off.

On the shield's inner face, scratched by its owner before the end:
They sing every night. They sing my name now. I never told them my name. Climbed up for the wall and the words on it. Should have stayed down by Hag Rock with the bard and his drum. If you are reading this you climbed too. Go back down.

notes.title: Climber's Last Page
notes.author: Svari the Bold
pages:
#28th of Sun's Height
Made the climb from the Hag Rock side. The wall of the dead at the top is real, carved with dragon claws. I put my hand on it and the stone was warm. One of the words shone, I swear it, and my head filled with a sound like a crowd running.

#29th
The crones found me. One of them laughed and said the Nords who made the wall were too frightened to read it. I'm hiding in the old tower. Heard a lute being played below. No bard alive would come here. So who's playing?

purewater_run.hook: A clear stream tumbles from a cave in the hills south of Markarth. The water is the sweetest in the Reach, and the den above it is full of things that think so too.
purewater_run.rumour: Purewater Run's water'll cure a hangover and a heartache both, the old women say. You just have to get past what's living in the cave above it.

notes.title: Herbalist's Gathering Notes
notes.author: Bryling, herb-woman of Markarth
pages: Purewater Run, by the falls: river betty, abundant. Mountain flower, blue and purple. Water drawn from the source spring keeps a potion fresh twice as long as Karth water, I do not know why.

Do not go into the cave. Something lives there with a large appetite and a Reachman's patience. Forsworn have been seen collecting water at dawn, carrying it south in hide bags toward Hag Rock. Someone among them is ill, I think, or someone is brewing something that needs pure water. Briars are thirsty things.

fort_sungard.hook: A Nordic fort on the eastern edge of the Reach, abandoned by the Legion and claimed by deserters who still wear its colours and still collect its taxes.
fort_sungard.rumour: Fort Sungard's got Legion banners and Legion armour, but don't let that fool you. Those are deserters, and they tax the road worse than any Jarl.

notes.title: Commander's Log, Fort Sungard
notes.author: Vatrius Hollow, 'Commander'
pages:
#Sun's Height, 4E 201
The Legion forgets its forts faster than it forgets its debts. Sungard was given up after the Markarth business. I, Vatrius Hollow, once optio of the Fourth Cohort, have taken it back for the Empire. The Empire does not know. The Empire will not be told.

#Last Seed
Taxed the road from the Bilegulch Mine: 80 septims and a cart of iron. The Orcs did not like it. The Orcs can complain to the Emperor.
The cohort's eagle standard hangs in the hall. As long as it hangs there, we are not deserters. We are a garrison. It is important to the men to believe this. It is important to me.

notes.title: Complaint to the Jarl of Markarth
notes.author: Alding, wagoner of Rorikstead
pages:
My Jarl,
The 'Legion' at Fort Sungard charged me 30 septims to pass a road the Empire paid for. When I asked for a receipt, the commander gave me one, written very neatly, signed 'Vatrius Hollow, Commander, Sungard Garrison, on behalf of His Imperial Majesty'.
I took it to the Legion camp near Bthardamz. The tribune laughed for a long time, then stopped, and asked me which way the fort was.

The Jarl's steward has written across the bottom: Forwarded to the Legion. The Legion replies that Fort Sungard is not a Legion fort and Vatrius Hollow is not a Legion officer, and that they would be very grateful if someone would remove the eagle standard from his hall before anyone in Solitude hears of it.

gloomreach.hook: A cave in the southeastern Reach where glowing fungus lights the walls in green and blue, and the Falmer tend their gardens in the dark.
gloomreach.rumour: There's mushrooms down in Gloomreach that glow like moons. Alchemists'll pay a fortune for them. The pale folk who farm them don't sell.

notes.title: Letter to an Alchemist in Markarth
notes.author: Sinnoc, spore-gatherer
pages: Master Lisbet, the spores are everything I promised. Glowing caps the size of a shield. I've filled one satchel already and I'm going deeper for the blue ones, the kind you said cure a fever in a night.

Should I not come back, the satchel is hidden behind the second falls, under a flat stone with a chalk mark. You paid me in advance, so you're owed it, dead or alive. I'm a lot of things, master, but I'm not a cheat.
The Falmer are tending these things like a farmer tends his beans. I think there is one who does nothing else. They call him something that sounds like a hiss.

notes.title: Chalk Drawings on a Cave Wall
pages:
On the walls of the deepest grotto someone, likely Sinnoc, has copied the Falmer scratchings in chalk to understand them. They show rows of mushrooms, carefully counted. Then a figure holding a staff over them. Then the figure feeding something to the mushrooms: something with arms and legs.
Under the drawing, in Sinnoc's hand: Oh. That's what the soil is.

Further along the wall the chalk lines grow shaky. Sinnoc has drawn the Falmer gardener again, larger, with something around its neck, a cord strung with what might be teeth. Beside it he has written: He wears the gatherers he catches. I can see a Nord ring on that cord. I am going back for my satchel and then I am leaving.

valthume.hook: A sealed Nordic barrow in the hills south of Old Hroldan, where the dead of an ancient war were buried with their weapons and, some say, their oaths still unbroken.
valthume.rumour: Ulfgar the Lamp-Keeper at Old Hroldan tells a story about Valthume and the ghost in his inn. The story's long. The ale's cheap. Go on.

notes.title: Letter Sealed in a Lead Tube
notes.author: Sigrun, innkeeper of Old Hroldan, 3E 412
pages:
To whoever opens this tomb in a kinder age.
The soldier Ketil fought for Hjalti when Old Hroldan was taken. He died in my inn, in the upstairs room, with his shield still on his arm. The Reachmen's dead are buried here in Valthume and the Nords' dead were laid beside them, because there was no time to separate friend from foe.

Ketil's shield was taken into Valthume by mistake with the others. Since then he walks the upstairs room at night looking for it. He is a kind ghost. He fixes the shutters. But he is not at rest.
If you can bring his shield back to the inn, hang it on the wall above the bed. My family will keep the lamp lit for him until then. I have made my children swear it.

notes.title: Ward Stone at the Inner Hall
pages:
Rendered from the ancient runes:
Here lie together Reach and Nord, for the war ended at the grave's edge and not before. Let none who sleep here wake to fight again.
Someone has carved beneath it, much later: The dead did not listen. The warden of this hall still fights, and every shield in the barrow is his now. He will not give them back. You will have to take them.

Lower still, faint and recent: Ketil's shield is the round one with the hawk painted on it, faded nearly away. I saw it on the warden's arm as he passed me in the dark. He was holding it the way a man holds a stolen thing he means to keep. I did not ask him to give it back. You may have more courage than I did.

cradle_stone_tower.hook: A broken stone tower on a crag near Bard's Leap, its base worn smooth by ages of Reachfolk mothers who came to lay their newborns on the rock for a blessing.
cradle_stone_tower.rumour: The Reachfolk used to bring their babies to the Cradle Stone for luck. The Forsworn hold it now. Not much luck to go round these days.

notes.title: Blessing Painted on the Cradle Stone
pages:
In ochre on the flat stone at the tower's foot, in the Reach tongue, copied and translated by a wandering scholar:
Child of the Reach, here is the rock your mothers lay on. Be as hard. Here is the wind your fathers breathed. Be as free. Here is the river below. Be as patient. It cut this valley with nothing but time.

The scholar adds: The Forsworn who now hold the tower still bring infants here at the turn of the year, under guard. A sentry let me copy this on the condition that I wrote it truly. I believe I have.

notes.title: Bark Note from a Sentry
pages:
To the chief at Lost Valley. The crones there want the Cradle Stone for their rites. They want to bury briar here. I say no. The Cradle is for the living. Send me ten more spears and I will keep saying no.
The falls are loud this year. Something in Gloomreach is singing under the rock at night. Not Falmer. Falmer do not sing.

Below, a reply in a crone's spidery marks: Ten spears is ten spears less for the Nords. You will have three. And the briar will be buried where the briar is wanted. The Cradle is old, sentry, and old things serve the strong. Count your three spears and be grateful I do not count you.

bards_leap_summit.hook: A waterfall plunging from the cliffs by Lost Valley Redoubt, named for a bard who leapt from its top and lived to sing about it, or so the bards insist.
bards_leap_summit.rumour: Bards say if you leap from the top of Bard's Leap and live, you'll never be tongue-tied again. Bards also say a lot of things.

notes.title: Verse Carved on the Summit Rock
notes.author: Anonymous, signed 'the Leaper'
pages: ~I came up here with a broken heart,
~A broken lute, and a Briarheart's dart.
~I dropped my ring where the white water pours,
~Then I followed it down. The pool is yours.
^Below, smaller: The ring was Ingrith's. She married a merchant in Markarth. If you find it in the pool beneath the falls, keep it. I'm done with it. - the Leaper

Further down the rock, in a different and steadier hand: I watched him jump. He came up laughing in the pool with blood on his lip, and he sang the whole walk back to Markarth and never once stammered. Some of the Bards' College folk think the falls themselves are blessed. I think a man who survives that has nothing left to be nervous about.

lost_valley_redoubt.hook: A Forsworn stronghold built around the falls of Bard's Leap, where hagravens keep prisoners in cages over the water and a word wall broods on the heights.
lost_valley_redoubt.rumour: A minstrel from the College in Solitude was taken near Lost Valley Redoubt. They say the crones keep him singing for his supper. One wrong note and he's the supper.

notes.title: Pages from a Songbook
notes.author: Teodric of the Bards College
pages:
#Day 4 of captivity
The hagraven Kerath Burnt-Feather wants a new song every night. I have sung her every ballad I know and three I made up on the spot. She liked 'The Crone on the Crag'. Of course she did.

#Day 9
She is running out of patience and I am running out of songs. Tonight I sang 'Ragnar the Red' and she fed my lute to the fire. Tomorrow, she says, it's my turn.
If a hero reads this: the cages hang above the falls. The crone holds the keys in her claws. You'll have to take them off her.

notes.title: Bone-Scratched Tablet
notes.author: Kerath Burnt-Feather
pages:
The word on the wall above says something about winds. The Nords who carved it would not tell. Dragons speak only to dragons, and to the Dragonborn, whatever that is.
The singer is useful. Songs are a kind of magic. If I learn the shape of his songs I will put it in a briar and make a Briarheart who sings men's courage out of them. Dead Crone Rock will envy me.

A second tablet, broken across:
The Nord's songs have no magic in them, only cleverness. Cleverness is not nothing. He tricked a sentry into opening his cage with a song about a key. I fed the sentry to the falls. The singer I keep. A creature that sings its way out of a cage is worth more than a dozen who only scream.

sky_haven_temple.hook: Behind the Karthspire, carved deep into the mountain, lies an ancient sanctuary of the Blades from the days of Reman. Its dragon-faced door has not opened in centuries.
sky_haven_temple.rumour: There's a story about a door in the cliffs behind Karthspire with a dragon's face on it. Won't open for picks, won't open for spells. Waiting for someone, I suppose.

notes.title: Akaviri Script by the Approach
pages:
Carved in a flowing foreign script beside the stair, with a Tamrielic gloss in a much later and more careful hand:
WE WERE THE WATCHERS OF THE DRAGON'S BLOOD. WE KEPT OUR VIGIL HERE WHEN THE EMPIRE FORGOT THE SKY.

The gloss continues: The Blades who left this here believed the dragons would return and that only one of dragon blood could stand against them. Most of Skyrim thought them fools. In the last year, Skyrim has been revising its opinion.

the_lover_stone.hook: An ancient standing stone in the Reach hills, blessed by the Lover constellation. Couples come to it to pledge themselves, and some leave letters for those who never came.
the_lover_stone.rumour: Young folk from Karthwasten meet at the Lover Stone, even Nords and Reachfolk, if you can believe it. There's a letter tucked under the stone right now, if the gossip's right.

notes.title: Letter Tucked Beneath the Stone
notes.author: Aiwen of the Karth
pages:
Leif,
You did not come on the night of the new moon. I waited until the frost was on my hair. Then my mother's people came and I had to go with them.
I am leaving you my braided token. It is the only thing I own that is mine and not my clan's. My mother says I am promised to the crones at Blind Cliff Cave. Do not come for me. I mean it.

I do not mean it. Come for me.
No. Do not. You are a miner's son from Karthwasten with a pick and a kind face and they would eat you alive.
Keep the token. Remember me by it. The Lover's blessing go with you, wherever it goes. - A.

notes.title: Words Worn into the Stone's Base
pages:
Ancient Nordic letters, barely readable, worn by hands and weather:
UNDER THE LOVER, ALL ARE ONE BLOOD.
Carved beneath in a dozen hands, some old and some fresh: initials joined with lines. H and S. B and T. Two Reach marks joined to a Nord rune. A and L, the newest, the lines still pale in the stone.

Someone has left a small offering at the foot of the stone: a sprig of mountain flower, a copper ring and a wooden spoon carved with a hawk. A scrap of bark tied to the spoon reads, in a careful Nord hand: For A. I came on the second night. You were already gone. I will keep coming. - L.

word_wall_dead_crone_rock.hook: On the cliffs beside Dead Crone Rock stands a curving wall of dragon script, its claw-marked words still faintly humming with power.
word_wall_dead_crone_rock.rumour: Old Nord wall up past Dead Crone Rock, covered in dragon scratches. They say it teaches a word that makes grown men run screaming. Useful, around crones.

notes.title: Translation Chalked Beside the Wall
notes.author: A traveller who did not sign
pages:
My best attempt at the dragon script, worked out with a College primer and a great deal of guessing:
HERE THE DRAGON'S SERVANTS LAID THE BRAVE WHO DID NOT FLINCH, AND FEAR ITSELF WAS SET TO GUARD THEM, SO THAT THE LIVING WOULD STAY AWAY.

One word glowed as I read it, a word I think means 'fear' or 'dismay'. When I touched it I felt like a man at the edge of a cliff, about to fall. I left in a hurry. Whoever comes next: put your hand on the brightest word. You'll know which one.

dragon_mound_the_lover_stone.hook: An ancient dragon burial mound in the hills between the Lover Stone and the Legion's camp. Its stones have been pushed outward from within.
dragon_mound_the_lover_stone.rumour: The legionaries at the Reach camp won't stand watch facing that mound to the south. Say it moved. Say something climbed out of it. They're soldiers, not poets, so maybe it's true.

notes.title: Sentry's Report, Reach Imperial Camp
notes.author: Legionary Fulvia Mox
pages: Sir, I was on night watch on the 9th of Frostfall. At the third bell the ground to the south shook. I saw the stones of the burial mound fly apart and something large rise out of it, black against the stars.

It flew north over the camp. It did not attack. It did not need to. I have been told to write that I saw a large bird. I saw a large bird, sir. A large bird that roared in words I could feel in my teeth. Request a transfer to Cyrodiil, sir.

dragon_mound_harmugstahl.hook: A dragon burial mound in the high hills north of Harmugstahl. Robed figures have been seen chanting over its broken stones by moonlight.
dragon_mound_harmugstahl.rumour: Folks in Karthwasten have seen robed men chanting at the old mound north of Harmugstahl. Dragon worshippers, in this day and age. Nothing good ever came of praying to something with teeth.

notes.title: Sermon of the Returning Wing
notes.author: Brother Valmund, of the Returning Wing
pages: Brothers, the masters return. The mound at Dragontooth Crater is empty. The mound at the Lover Stone is empty. The dragon priests of old were not fools, they were wise, and we shall be wise again.

This mound has not yet opened. The master inside sleeps deeper than the rest. We shall wake him with blood and chanting, and when he rises, he will remember who knelt first.
Bring the shepherds from Karthwasten. Bring the goats if you cannot find shepherds. The master is not particular, or so I hope.

dragon_mound_karthspire.hook: A broken dragon burial mound on the slopes below the Karthspire. Whatever slept inside it has already risen, and the scorched earth around it has not yet regrown.
dragon_mound_karthspire.rumour: The mound below Karthspire burst open in the spring. Miners at Soljund's Sinkhole saw a dragon fly out of it like a hawk from a box. Haven't slept well since.

notes.title: Letter from Soljund's Sinkhole
notes.author: Hrefna, mine clerk
pages:
Dear cousin in Whiterun,
You laughed at me when I wrote about dragons. Laugh at this: on the 14th of Second Seed, the mound below Karthspire split open like an egg. A huge black dragon circled above it, shouting down into the earth, and then a second dragon dug its way up out of the ground and they both flew off toward Sky Haven.

Pa says the Forsworn at Karthspire Camp were so frightened they came down to the mine and asked to shelter with us. We let them. They slept in the lower gallery. They've gone now. The dragon hasn't come back. Neither has my good sense.
